text: For a long time, a terrible disease called the Red Death had swept across the country, and no plague had ever been so deadly. <break time="0.8s" /> Its mark was red, for scarlet spots on the face showed that a person had caught it. <break time="0.8s" /> The whole illness, from the first signs to the end, took only half an hour, and no one could help the sick. <break time="0.8s" /> But Prince Prospero, the ruler of the land, was happy and fearless, and he was also clever in his own way. <break time="0.8s" /> When half of his people had died, he invited a thousand healthy, cheerful friends from among his knights and ladies. <break time="0.8s" /> With them he went away to one of his castles, a huge and magnificent building surrounded by a strong, high wall. <break time="0.8s" /> The gates were made of iron, and the courtiers sealed the bolts with fire and heavy hammers so that no one could get in or out. <break time="0.8s" /> There was plenty of food inside, and the prince believed that the world outside could take care of itself. <break time="0.8s" /> He had brought clowns, dancers, musicians, beauty, and wine, and it seemed foolish to feel sad or even to think. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside the walls there was safety, but outside them was the Red Death.
